newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar recoups earlier losses vs yen by late Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar recoups earlier losses vs yen by late Tokyo.

text.p: 0628 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT

The dollar pared earlier losses against the yen by late Tokyo on Friday after falling on comments by a senior official of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) on the possibility of credit-tightening by Japan.
Depite a brief dip on the rate rise fears, dealers said the dollar was bought back quickly amid a growing market perception that an imminent rise in Japenese rates is unlikely.
Koji Omi, deputy chairman of the LDP's Policy Research Council, told Reuters: "There is a chance of an interest rate increase by early autumn as economic fundamentals are getting better."

The dollar fell as low as 116.12 yen as his comments circulated in the market, but dealers said traders took his comments as an excuse to sell dollars, while short-covering from domestic and overseas operators soon emerged. "It could be just political talk... Expectations for an imminent rate increase have faded after weak industrial production output data (on Thursday)," a trust bank dealer said.
Separately, an official with the LDP administrative reform panel said told Reuters on Friday it will recommend that the Japanese government raise interest rates in the future.
"People are having a hard time as a result of low interest rates... We would like to call on the government to show more consideration to this situation," the official said.

Dealers said, however, that the market still doubts if the central bank is ready to raise the official discount rate anytime soon amid recent weak economic data and worries about Japan's financial system, which were again highlighted by the arrest of the former president of Nomura Securites on Thursday.
Some Japanese trust banks were said to be eager to purchase dollars for yen on dips, making the dollar's downside solid near 116.10 yen, dealers said.
On the topside, exporter offers and possible option-linked sales above 116.60 yen, along with hedge sales by investors, had weighed on the dollar, dealers said.

"Some speculative accounts have also unwound their long positions on the topside, keeping the dollar top-heavy, while no strong buying incentives were detected today," a city bank dealer said. Dealers say the greenback is likely to remain in a range of roughly 115 to 117 yen for a while.
Singapore dealers said the dollar appeared to have settled into a range, as most participants had squared their positions ahead of Sunday's French elections.

A dealer at a U.S. bank said although a win by the left in Sunday's decisive ballot could spark purchases of marks for the French franc, perceptions of possible weakening of the euro following victory by the left could lead to dollar purchases against the mark, making the mark's future direction unclear.
The dollar closed at about 116.30 yen and 1.6972 marks in New York on Thursday. -- Singapore newsroom +65-8703080, Yoko Nishikawa in Tokyo +81-3-3432-8548
